primitives.verbatim_quote: The system includes an inertial navigation system (INS) module first state module adapted for measuring parameters associated with the object state, a wireless transmitter, a battery for providing electric power, and a mounting module connecting the object with the first state module, the wireless transmitter and the battery.
primitives.assumptions: Local inertial frame assumed constant; drift negligible over short intervals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High acceleration or rotation rates exceeding sensor dynamic range.

primitives.name: Vision-Based Tracking System
primitives.verbatim_quote: The camera system capturing the object includes at least two mutually displaced camera clusters, and each camera cluster includes one or more cameras for providing a predetermined spatial resolution.

primitives.name: Global Positioning System Module
primitives.verbatim_quote: The system may include a global positioning system (GPS) module which provides the independent data relating to the object state.

The system integrates three primary sensing modalities—INS, vision, and GPS—to compute object state dynamically. INS provides high-frequency kinematic feedback but suffers from drift; vision offers rich geometric context but depends on lighting and visibility; GPS delivers absolute positioning but can be unreliable indoors or in obstructed areas. These components form a dual structure where INS drives short-term prediction, vision refines pose accuracy, and GPS corrects long-term bias. The fusion process involves Kalman filtering or particle filtering to combine these heterogeneous signals into a coherent estimate of object state (position, orientation, velocity). Failure modes arise when any modality fails (e.g., GPS outage, camera occlusion), leading to degraded performance unless fallback mechanisms are engaged. The mathematical duality lies in the complementary nature of these sensors: INS is temporal, vision is spatial, and GPS is referential. Their interplay defines a robust tracking kernel suitable for real-time applications such as ball tracking in sports.
